ayahOccurrences.text: أَوَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتِيَهُم بَأْسُنَا ضُحًى وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: أَوَأَمِنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ أَن يَأْتِيَهُم بَأْسُنَا ضُحًى وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ

ayahOccurrences.text: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى

ayahOccurrences.text: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا۟ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَىٰ

ayahOccurrences.text: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوٓا۟ إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوٓا۟ إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: ضُحًى is in the derivative form: ضُحَى
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ض/ح/و   ḍ–ḥ–w the breaking of day, daylight, the brief time of mid‐morning, to enter at the time of mid‐morning, to expose oneself to the sun; to appear, to appear conspicuously; suburb and surroundings; sacrificial animal, to sacrifice.

Of this root, 2 forms occur 7 times in the Qur’an:
تَضْحَى taḍḥā 1 time and ضُحَى ḍuḥā 6 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
ضُحَى ḍuḥā [n.]

1 mid‐morning, forenoon

(20:59)‏وَأَنْ‏ ‏يُحْشَرَ‏ ‏النَّاسُ‏ ‏ضُحًى‏ and that people be assembled at forenoon; *

(79:46)‏لَمْ‏ ‏يَلْبَثُوا‏ ‏إِلاَّ‏ ‏عَشِيَّةً‏ ‏أَوْ‏ ‏ضُحَاهَا they have not tarried but a very short time [lit. an evening or the mid‐morning following it]; * الضُحَىname of Sura 91, Meccan sura, so-named because of the reference in verse

1 to ‘Mid‐Morning Brightness’

2 sunlight

(91:1) وَالشَّمْسِ‏ ‏وَضُحَاهَا‏ ‏ by the sun and its light

3 daylight ‏

(79:29) ‏وَأَغْطَشَ‏ ‏لَيْلَهَا‏ ‏وَأَخْرَجَ‏ ‏ضُحَاهَا and He gave darkness to its [the sky’s] night, and brought out its daylight.

entries.label: تَضْحَى
entries.definitionHtml:
تَضْحَى taḍḥā [imperf. v., intrans.] to be exposed to the heat of the sun

(20:119)‏ وَأَنَّكَ‏ ‏لاَ‏ ‏تَظْمَأُ‏ ‏فِيهَا‏ولا تَضْحَى‏‏ and you will never [in the Garden] suffer thirst nor the heat of the sun.
